meta.title: Ch 14: Special Features of Audit of Banks & NBFCs — MCQ Bank
meta.description: Chapter-wise practice MCQs for Chapter 14 (Special Features of Audit of Banks & NBFCs).

questions.q: Restructured accounts still 'standard' + interest accruing — the risk direction:
o: Classification only
Overstatement of income AND understated provisioning — both from the same misclassification; quantify the effect on both profit and capital
Cash-flow risk
Understatement of assets
questions.why: One error, two wounds: the restructures (if they failed RBI qualifying criteria) must be downgraded ⇒ provisioning; accrued interest on classified accounts must be suspended ⇒ income overstated — the auditor books the correction to both lines, and the CRAR consequence follows the provision.
questions.trend: Fits the style in which ICAI drafts RTP/MTP questions on this topic (pattern estimate; no guarantee of appearance).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Misclassification pays a double fine — profit and capital The same rust dents both the hull and the gauge.

questions.stem: Rural branch audit of AgriBank: 140 loan accounts above threshold reviewed; the auditor finds: 12 accounts restructured last year are still shown 'standard' with interest accruing; 6 accounts show repayments funded by a fresh cash-credit limit dated the same day; the concurrent-audit report flagged three of these in October and management's reply says 'compliance will be ensured'.

questions.q: The same-day repaid-by-new-limit pattern is:
o: Recovery! Good for the bank
Borrowing-to-repay (evergreening) — a classic NPA-concealment; evaluate the realisation: no new money reached the borrower's business; re-age the accounts from the original default
Normal working capital practice
Only a compliance issue
questions.why: A 'repayment' funded by the same facility is not a repayment: the fresh disbursement was not a genuine new facility on merit (the fund-flow check) — reclassify by the substance of when the account was genuinely served, and treat the pattern as a fraud-risk indicator (management override to show standard-book cleanliness).
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — this topic stays active in ICAI question-setting Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

mem.tip: Follow the money, not the teller entry A loan washing its own hands stays dirty.

questions.q: The concurrent-audit report's ignored flags mean:
o: No change to the statutory audit — that's internal
Reliance on internal/concurrent work shifts; these known issues become DIRECT test targets, and management inaction informs the integrity/override risk picture
Trust management's reply
Report to the AGM
questions.why: The statutory auditor reads concurrent/CAC audit reports and their status of compliance; unremediated known flags = high-risk items with prior notice — the audit response escalates from sample to full check on those accounts, and management's inaction feeds the fraud-risk and ICFR judgments (a 'significant deficiency' pattern).

questions.q: For provisioning, the auditor tests the classification file against:
o: Last year's list
The loan ledger's actual overdue ageing and the RBI restructure/monitoring criteria — recompute, don't tick
The board's comfort
The shareholding pattern

questions.q: The auditor's report to the bank's audit committee should frame the three findings as:
o: Three unrelated errors

A pattern of asset-quality overstatement: provisioning, income recognition, and concealment indicators together, with the CRAR implication — and the fraud-reporting consideration at the scale thresholds
A technical reclassification
A training gap
questions.why: Individually 'technical'; together a systemic bias in the same direction, at a branch where someone was told in October — the reporting answer names the aggregate (income + capital), the pattern, and the next duty (fraud-reporting route once the amount test is met, per the 143(12) framework).

questions.q: For an NBFC, the audit emphasis on asset classification should rely on:
o: Management's certificate on standard-asset status
Overdue days per the loan ledger (90-day NPA trigger, current-account method nuances included) and provisioning adequacy
Last year's classification
Rating agency reports
questions.why: The RBI-observed 90-day overdue NPA trigger (with the current-account method for lump-sum due and specific loan-card logic) is the classification core; the auditor tests the ageing, not the assertion; provisioning follows the graded sub-standard/doubtful/loss rules.

questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — age the ledger, never trust the certificate AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Days overdue are the only calendar auditors read.

questions.q: A bank audit's PSL check requires verifying achievement of:
o: 40% of ANBC to priority sector (with 18% agriculture / 10% weaker sections tiers) and classification of eligible borrowers, or disclosure of shortfall with the priority sector lending certificate scheme handling
18% to agriculture only
4% CRR on net demand
9% CAR per exposure
questions.why: PSL targets (40% overall/18% agri/10% weaker sections for foreign banks' Indian branches are exempt overall but 40% domestic banks etc. — study the current master direction; exam level: the triad of ratios, borrower eligibility, and shortfall instruments (PSLC purchase) — the auditor reconciles the return to the loan book; unsecured lending beyond thresholds and reclassification of diversion matter more than the certificate.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Lower likelihood but possible — the numbers to know for sure: the 40/18/10 triad — check notifications Included so a low-probability surprise cannot catch you cold.

questions.why: 90 days (current duenot overdue) is the NPA trigger; further ageing then drives the sub-standard→doubtful→loss ladder.

questions.q: Bank/NBFC provisioning must be tested by recomputing from:
o: The classification tag in the register
The overdue ageing data and the applicable provisioning rates
Last year's figure
Management's note
questions.why: The register's tag is an assertion; the ageing is the fact — the auditor recomputes classification from dues, then applies the graded provisions.

questions.q: The scale-based regulation for NBFCs re-sets audit attention mainly via:
o: Uniform rules
Tiered entity classes (materiality, governance and disclosure obligations scaled to size/systemic importance) — the audit's depth follows the tier
Only listed NBFCs
No audit relevance
questions.why: REGULATORY shift: the tiering (base/middle/upper) changes which NBFCs face enhanced prudential and reporting norms — and therefore the audit scope, provisioning intensity, and governance expectations to test in the middle/upper layers.
questions.trend: Documented syllabus/amendment change — applicability from May 2026 exam onwards per ICAI BoS announcement.
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — regulation now has a size dial AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Big pools, deeper rules — audit accordingly.

questions.q: The bank auditor's reconciliation task between regulatory returns and financial statements exists because:
o: They must differ by design
Prudential (RBI) and accounting frameworks diverge on provisioning, income and classification — the bridge explains the differences, and unexplained gaps are misstatement or regulatory risk
The returns are optional
The FS use different currency
questions.why: Divergent recognition (regulatory provisioning vs Ind AS ECL, income suspension rules) means the two books legitimately part ways — the auditor's job is the reconciliation and the labels: unexplained difference = wrong either way.
questions.trend: Known trap zone: ICAI objective papers repeatedly test limits/exceptions of this rule (pattern estimate).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — two rulebooks, one truth line AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: The bridge between the two balance sheets IS the audit workpaper.
mem.link: Chapter 14 — Special Features of Audit of Banks & NBFCs

questions.q: Testing prudential exposure ceilings for 'practically linked' borrower groups requires the auditor to:
o: Count only named legal entities
Trace common management/control/fund flows to aggregate exposure — related parties in all but name defeat the limit
Accept the client's classification
Ask the rating agency
questions.why: Prudential limits bind the group exposure; borrower-group identification (common directors, cash pooling, inter-corporate deposits) is a test of substance: the register's name isn't the obligor's limit.

questions.q: A term loan's instalment is overdue 780 days at the reference date. Classification under the 90-day NPA rule:
o: Doubtful
Always Sub-standard on any overdue
Standard — 90 days is only for disclosure
Loss asset regardless of ageing
questions.why: NPA triggers beyond 90 days overdue (780 ⇒ NPA — beyond 1 year of NPA status ⇒ doubtful territory); note 'current-account method' rules for lump-sum accounts (overdraft balance 90 days) in the full standard.

mem.tip: 90 days overdue ⇒ NPA at inception (sub-standard); further 12 months ⇒ doubtful; loss on identification — ageing drives both class and provisioning.

questions.q: A bank's ANBC is Rs 50,000 lakh; net PSL advance Rs 16,000 lakh. RBI's 40% PSL target ⇒ audit position:
o: Excess of Rs 4,000 lakh to lend to weaker sections
Shortfall is cured by reclassifying any loan
Shortfall Rs 4,000 lakh ⇒ purchase PSLCs of equal amount (if it opts); the cost of the certificate scheme vs re-lending is the management decision
PSLCs are bought for the AGRI target only
questions.why: 40% of ANBC = 20,000 vs actual 16,000 ⇒ shortfall 4,000 lakh — PSLC route (purchase in the subordinate market) or accept the penalty framing.
questions.trend: No dominant past-pattern signal; included for balanced coverage (AI judgement).
questions.probWhy: Realistic likelihood for Nov 2026 — the 40% test plus certificate mechanics is bank-audit numeracy AI prediction, not a certainty.

mem.tip: Shortfall vs the 40% PSL target is closed by purchasing PSL certificates (aggregate shortfall at bank level), then re-lending at priority rates — the flow that changes the balance-sheet.
